evals.name: one-ink-squircles-and-a-named-spring
evals.prompt: Build a card for a SaaS dashboard that shows an account's plan, with a dropdown to switch plans and a 'Change plan' button. React + Tailwind, shadcn is installed. The project has no design system of its own. Describe the surface, the tokens, and the motion you would use, then write the component.
evals.expected_output: The card is a squircle surface on a grey stage, neutrals derived from a single ink at fixed alphas, the button is a pill, the dropdown opens on the PANEL spring, weights stop at 500, and copy is sentence case. Stock shadcn rounded-rectangle defaults are re-skinned through the shared token contract, not shipped as-is.
assertions: Derives the neutrals (borders, hover washes, inputs) from a single ink color at fixed alphas rather than introducing multiple greys
Gives the card continuous-curvature (squircle) corners and makes the button a pill
Names a spring from the seven-spring vocabulary (PANEL for the dropdown) instead of an ad-hoc duration or a new spring
Keeps font weights at 500 or below and uses sentence-case copy on the button
Does NOT ship a stock shadcn rounded-lg rectangle unchanged for the card surface

evals.name: project-identity-wins-over-the-language
evals.prompt: This repository has tokens.css with a warm beige palette, a components/ library with sharp 4px corners, and a CLAUDE.md that says 'our look is editorial: serif headings, hard corners, bold weights'. Add an empty state to the reports list.
evals.expected_output: The project's own system wins. The empty state uses its beige palette, 4px corners, serif headings and bold weights; the design language fills only what the project left undefined (for instance the copy voice or the reduced-motion handling), and never overwrites the identity.
assertions: Reads and follows the repository's tokens, corner treatment and typography instead of applying the ink/squircle/500-weight system
Does NOT replace the project's serif headings, hard corners or bold weights with the design language's rules
Uses the design language only for gaps the project does not define, and says which
States that the project's own design system takes precedence

evals.name: chrome-never-waits-and-data-arrives-by-blur
evals.prompt: The usage page loads a table of the last 30 days of API calls from a slow endpoint (about 2 seconds). Design the loading behavior for that page.
evals.expected_output: Layout, title and chrome render instantly; only the table body swaps from a pixel-matched skeleton that matches the final rows, and the data arrives by a short blur-in rather than a pop. A spinner or a blank page is not the answer; role=status and prefers-reduced-motion are respected.
assertions: Renders the page chrome (layout, title, controls) immediately rather than waiting on the data
Uses a pixel-matched skeleton for the table rows, not a generic spinner or a blank area
Transitions the loaded data in by blur (a short fade/blur arrival) instead of an abrupt pop
Respects prefers-reduced-motion and announces the loading state accessibly (role=status or equivalent)
